---
title: "Accessibility statement"
---

This statement applies to the Computing with AI course site, the reading copy of
the material for the joint module between Southwest Jiaotong University and the
University of Leeds. It was prepared on 25 November 2026.

We want everyone on the module to be able to use this site. We aim to meet the
Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, WCAG 2.2, level AA, which is the
standard the UK Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications)
Accessibility Regulations 2018 require.

## What you can expect

- Every page states its language, and passages in Chinese are marked as Chinese
  so that a screen reader pronounces them correctly.
- Text and interface colours meet the AA contrast ratios (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for
  interface boundaries and focus indicators) in both the light and the dark
  theme. You can switch theme with the toggle on each page.
- You can use the whole site with a keyboard. The focus indicator is always
  visible.
- Links are underlined as well as coloured, so colour is not the only cue.
- Pages use headings in order, and each page has an in-page contents list.
- Every notebook is published as an ordinary web page of text, code and output,
  so a screen reader can read it from top to bottom.
- You can zoom the page to 200% without losing content or function.

## Known limitations

This is our current position, and we will update it as the site changes.

- **Not yet independently audited.** We have checked colour contrast
  automatically and tested with a keyboard, but a full audit with assistive
  technology has not yet been carried out. We therefore describe the site as
  partially compliant until that audit is done.
- **Charts and images in notebooks.** A figure produced by code may not have a
  text description. Where a figure carries information, the surrounding text or
  the code that draws it is meant to give the same information; where it does
  not, that is a fault we want to hear about.
- **Interactive widgets are not yet published.** The module will add
  interactive explanations. Each will be built from ordinary page elements rather
  than a drawing canvas, will work with a keyboard (for example arrow keys for a
  slider), and will have a text version that presents the same information as a
  table or as prose. This statement will be updated when the first one ships.
- **Code output.** Wide tables and long lines of output scroll sideways inside
  their own box rather than reflowing.

## Tell us about a problem

If you cannot use part of this site, or you need the material in another format,
tell the module teaching team. Report a problem by opening an issue in the
course repository, or tell your tutor. Say which page it is and what you were
trying to do, and we will aim to reply within five working days.

If you are not happy with our response and you are in the United Kingdom, you can
contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service (EASS). In Northern Ireland,
the Equality Commission for Northern Ireland is responsible for enforcement.

## Technical information

This site is built with Quarto and published on GitHub Pages. It relies on
HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Its accessibility depends on the following
technologies working with your browser and any assistive technology you use.
